newsitem.title: ECUADOR: 22 dead in U.S. cargo jet crash in Ecuadoran city.
newsitem.headline: 22 dead in U.S. cargo jet crash in Ecuadoran city.

text.p: At least 22 people were killed and 60 injured when a U.S.-owned Boeing 707 cargo plane caught fire and crashed into a densely populated poor district of an Ecuadoran city, officials said on Wednesday.

The jet bound for Miami with flowers and frozen fish ploughed through the Dolorosa neighbourhood of the Pacific coast city of Manta at 10:40 p.m. local time on Tuesday (0340 GMT on Wednesday), setting fire to houses.

The crew of four, including three Americans, died in the crash, but most of the victims were on the ground. The death toll was expected to rise as rescue workers began searching the crash site. They had to wait for daybreak because the crashing plane took out electricity lines.
"For now we have 22 dead," Red Cross chief Javier Reyes told Reuters, raising an earlier toll after a victim died of burns in a hospital.
"But we will begin picking through the rubble now so we expect that number to rise," police Lt. Marcelo Rocha said in Manta, 290 miles (480 km) southeast of Quito.
The plane belonged to Millon Air, a Miami-based cargo carrier owned by a Colombian family. The company had no immediate comment on the crash.

Flaming wreckage rained death on eight blocks of Dolorosa. Shocked witnesses told how one of the plane's engines exploded at low altitude just after takeoff from Manta airport. Flying chunks of machinery tore off roofs and crushed a church.

"We rushed out and saw it was ripping the roofs off all the houses," one witness said. "Two houses just before ours fell over and collapsed from the impact. Part of the wing ended up just near where we live. It had dragged all the houses down until it smashed into a restaurant. The owner was there and he was killed."
Reyes said all four crew, three Americans and a Colombian, died in the crash about six miles (10 km) from the airport of Manta, capital of Manabi province.
"The engine caught fire and that caused the accident," Rocha told Reuters. "The unofficial version says the cause of the accident was a mechanical failure."
Ecuador's President Abdala Bucaram declared a national day of mourning and flew to Manta to supervise rescue operations.

"This is a tragedy," he said on television. "We will be in Manta with some ministers soon to help the victims and try to repair the damage of this terrible accident, which has put all Ecuadoreans in mourning."

Before dawn, frightened Dolorosa residents picked through the darkness trying to find victims and identify the dead. Red Cross, civil defence and Air Force rescue teams joined them in scouring the area and laid out six corpses in a park strewn with wreckage; 14 dead were taken to the local morgue.
City hospitals ran short of medicine to treat so many severe burn patients and pleaded for supplies, while dealing with worried residents seeking news of relatives and friends.

Millon Air operates cargo flights, mostly by charter, to Latin American destinations. In April last year a Millon Air DC-8 overran a runway in Guatemala City and crashed into a shantytown, killing at least six people on the ground.
